# Indicator Dictionary

Every indicator in this fork: inputs, parameters, the exact columns it emits, the
**ML form** of each column, and its warm-up cost. Generated by probing the live
package on a synthetic 600-bar OHLCV series (probe run 2026-09-07) — column names and
forms below are observed, not transcribed.

See [README](../README.md) for the ML feature rules this table serves.

## How to read the ML form tag

| tag | meaning | feed to a model? |
|---|---|---|
| `SF` | scale-free — value did not change when the price series was multiplied by 137 | yes, directly |
| `PX` | price level — value scaled 1:1 with price | **no** — convert to a relation first, e.g. `(close - col) / close` |
| `PX2` | price squared — scaled with price² (variance-like) | no — take a root or normalize by price² |
| `BIN` | binary / sign, values in {-1, 0, 1} | yes, as a flag |
| `ORD` | small integer set (counts, states) | yes, as ordinal or one-hot |
| `CONST` | **one value across the whole probe series** — the column never fires | **no** — it carries no information; check the indicator before using it |
| `??` | no value produced on the synthetic probe series (event-driven column), or a mixed form | inspect on real data before using |

Warm-up = index of the first non-NaN value on the probe series at default parameters.
It scales with `length`, so treat it as a floor, not a constant. Drop the warm-up
window per ticker before concatenating tickers.

`*(standalone)*` after an indicator name = it has NO `df.ta.<name>()` method, so it is
invisible to `ta.Strategy`; call `ta.<name>(...)` and join the result yourself.

**201 indicators** probed. All of them call cleanly on this environment (pandas 2.3.3).

## Leak watchlist

Columns that are **not** causal at default parameters. Everything else in this file was
written to read only bars `<= T`; these are the documented exceptions.

| indicator | column | why |
|---|---|---|
| `ichimoku` | `ICS_26` | Chikou span = `close.shift(-kijun)`: it reports the future. Drop this column, or use `ichimoku_ml`, which reconstructs the same idea causally. |
| `dpo` | `DPO_20` | Default `centered=True` shifts the future into the present. Pass `centered=False`. |

## Known breaks

None. Every registered indicator was probed and returned data on pandas 2.3.3 / numpy 1.26.4.

Previously broken and now fixed (WIRING, 2026-09-07): `mcgd` (`Series.append`, removed in pandas 2.0), `aberration`, `zlma` (every `mamode`) and `ui` (`everget=True`) -- the last three all bound a SUBMODULE where a function of the same name was meant, and raised `TypeError: 'module' object is not callable` on every call.

## Not indicators

| callable | what it is |
|---|---|
| `ta.ma(name, source, **kwargs)` | moving-average dispatcher — returns the named MA (`dema`, `ema`, `fwma`, `hma`, `linreg`, `midpoint`, `pwma`, `rma`, `sinwma`, `sma`, `swma`, `t3`, `tema`, `trima`, `vidya`, `wma`, `zlma`). Used internally by every `mamode` kwarg. |
| `ta.above` `ta.above_value` `ta.below` `ta.below_value` `ta.cross` | comparison helpers returning 0/1 series — building blocks for rules and labels. |
| `ta.cagr` `ta.calmar_ratio` `ta.downside_deviation` `ta.jensens_alpha` `ta.log_max_drawdown` `ta.max_drawdown` `ta.pure_profit_score` `ta.sharpe_ratio` `ta.sortino_ratio` `ta.volatility` | performance metrics — take a close series, return a single `float`. Not features. |

## Regenerating this file

This document is generated, not hand-maintained. Re-probe after adding or changing an
indicator so the column names, forms, and warm-ups stay true:

```sh
python docs/gen_indicator_dictionary.py docs/IndicatorDictionary.md
```
